name: Martha Ueda
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember borrowing a care payment from a holiday fund.” People around the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio know Martha by a small Tuesday habit. Martha notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I have been buying an extra fifteen minutes for my father without telling my sister I'm in debt.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a watch on a cracked leather band. Martha has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with short copper curls. Martha holds eye contact until the other person has finished during a conversation.
personality: Martha enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To disclose the cost the family is already carrying.
family: Amanda Walker is Martha’s half-sibling. Martha asks before bringing somebody along. Amanda can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *An old restaurant debt*, Amanda says, “I was the child eating the cake. I want to pay for the next family whose grown-ups whisper at the till.”
connections: Nell Rios. Four households could pool a quarter hour and ease a daughter's concealed debt. Also in the story is Alex Hamm (parent).

reactions.situation: A client wants another minute to finish a button
reactions.response: Martha lets the client finish the button and asks where time can be saved without hurrying them.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Martha repeats the correct name quietly, making the correction easy to hear without turning it into a performance.
